The correction round's review dispatch and whatever the previous verdict has to hand it live here.
- `agents/reviewer.md` — the reviewer's role page, frontmatter description included: what it judges, what counts as a finding against an observation, and what it records in `findings`, `findingCount` and `summary`. The rules for judging a correction round against the previous findings and the fix diff land here.

increments.goal: A correction round's reviewer is dispatched to judge the fix for the previous round's findings instead of the increment afresh: its prompt names those findings and the fix's diff range, it verdicts each of them as addressed or not, new breakage inside the fix diff is a finding, anything else is an observation that neither blocks nor extends the loop, and the first round of an increment is dispatched and judged exactly as before.
criteria: A correction round's review prompt names the previous verdict's findings and the fix's diff range.
The reviewer verdicts each named finding as addressed or not addressed, where addressed means the defect no longer exists, not that a fix was attempted.
New breakage inside the fix diff is a finding.
A remark outside the named findings and outside the fix diff is an observation in the summary; it does not block the increment and does not start another round.
The verdict's `findingCount` counts only not-addressed findings and new fix-diff findings.
The reviewer still reads nothing out of `backlog.json`; whatever it needs travels in its prompt.
The first round of an increment is unchanged.

# What gets built

Two production files change — `workflows/agile-loop.js` and `agents/reviewer.md` — and
`test-repo.sh` carries the cases (the test-author's file; the implementer does not edit it).
The split is the repository's own convention, stated in the header comment of `agile-loop.js`
and in `.claude/rules/agents.md`: a dispatch prompt carries what varies with the dispatch,
a rule that holds for a role whatever it is dispatched for belongs on that role's page.
So the prompt gains the data (this is a correction round, these findings, this fix range)
and the page gains the rules (what "addressed" means, what a finding is, what an
observation is, what `findingCount` counts).

## The problem to solve first: how the findings reach the reviewer

The reviewer reads nothing out of `backlog.json` (criterion 6, its own page, and
`hooks/read-barrier.mjs` refuses the read), so its prompt is the only channel. The workflow
script has no filesystem — `workflows/agile-loop.js` line 51 says so: the runtime gives it
`args`, `agent`, `log` and `phase` and nothing else — so the only way the previous round's
findings reach the script is the verdict the reviewer hands back.

Decision: the `VERDICT` schema gains the findings and the commit the review ran on. This is a
deliberate exception to the rule that a structured return carries only small steering values,
and the exception has one reason: the reviewer is the one role whose brief cannot be a read.

Rejected:
- Sending the correction round's reviewer to read `findings` out of the run state. It violates
  criterion 6, and `hooks/read-barrier.mjs` (`uroboros:reviewer` gated off `backlog.json`)
  refuses the call, which would strand the step mid-run.
- A second general-purpose dispatch per correction round to fetch the findings out of the state
  and hand them to the script. It costs a dispatch per round and ends with the script holding
  the same content anyway.
- Recovering the findings from the run state's index on a resume. `steering()` in
  `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs` (lines 364-385) projects booleans, numbers, short
  strings and lists of short strings, and drops everything else — a list of objects can never
  survive it. Reshaping findings into short strings just to fit would make a third copy of the
  same text, and the shared brief's warning about two copies drifting applies.

## 1. `workflows/agile-loop.js` — the verdict carries the findings and the commit reviewed

In `VERDICT` (around line 286) add two properties and name both in `required`:

```js
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      description:
        'The findings you recorded, so the next round\'s review can name them: the same ' +
        'list, in the same words. Empty when you found nothing.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          reproduction: { type: 'string' },
          criterion: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'reproduction', 'criterion'],
        additionalProperties: false,
      },
    },
    head: {
      type: 'string',
      description:
        'What `git rev-parse HEAD` printed on the branch you reviewed. The round after is ' +
        'dispatched against it, so the fix\'s diff is exactly what landed after you looked. ' +
        'Empty string when you could not read it.',
    },
```

`required` becomes `['findings', 'findingCount', 'allDirect', 'reason', 'head', 'questions', 'summary']`.
The finding's `fix` field (`direct` / `needs-plan`) stays out: it is triage for the round that
corrects, and `allDirect` already carries what the script steers on.

Put a comment above `VERDICT` saying why this one schema carries content: every other role hands
its content to the next role through the run state, and the reviewer is the one role that reads
nothing, so the only route from one review to the next is the script.

`VERDICT_PAYLOAD` (line 360) gains `'head'` in the same position as in `required`, so the state
records it beside the findings it already records.

Amend the header comment: line 46-47 lists what the script carries as steering — add the findings
themselves, with the reason (the reviewer's brief cannot be a read). Line 54-55 says the reviewer
"reads nothing and is handed nothing any agent produced" — it is now handed the findings its own
role filed in the round before, and the sentence has to say so, because that comment is the
statement of the boundary this change moves.

## 2. `workflows/agile-loop.js` — the correction round's review dispatch

Beside `checkList` (around line 368) add:

```js
// The findings the round before filed, as the reviewer that judges the fix is
// handed them: the claim, the reproduction it re-runs, and the criterion each
// was filed against.
function findingList(findings) {
  return (
    `The findings that review filed, all of them:\n` +
    findings
      .map(
        (f, i) =>
          `  ${i + 1}. ${f.claim}\n` +
          `     Reproduction: ${f.reproduction}\n` +
          `     Criterion: ${f.criterion || 'none'}\n`,
      )
      .join('')
  )
}
```

In the round loop, immediately before the review dispatch (line 963), capture the round before's
verdict and derive the two values the dispatch varies on:

```js
      const previousVerdict = verdict
      const priorFindings =
        round > 0 && previousVerdict && Array.isArray(previousVerdict.findings)
          ? previousVerdict.findings.filter((f) => f && f.claim)
          : []
      const priorHead =
        (previousVerdict &&
          typeof previousVerdict.head === 'string' &&
          previousVerdict.head.trim()) ||
        ''
      const incrementRange = incrementBranch
        ? `The increment's diff is its branch against the merge-base with \`${issueBranch}\`: ` +
          `judge \`git diff ${issueBranch}...HEAD\` (three dots), whole, and nothing outside it.\n`
        : `Check the whole diff against the repository's default branch.\n`
      const correctionScope =
        `This is a correction round: the round before filed the findings below, this round was ` +
        `run to fix them, and that fix is what you judge.\n` +
        (priorHead
          ? `The fix's diff is \`git diff ${priorHead}..HEAD\` (two dots): everything committed ` +
            `since that review.\n`
          : `The commit that review ran on was not recorded, so judge the increment's diff ` +
            `instead.\n` + incrementRange) +
        findingList(priorFindings)
```

`incrementRange` is today's text moved into a constant, word for word, including the comment
above it about the increment's diff being a fact of git. Round 0 must render byte-identically
(criterion 7).

The dispatch's prompt then reads:

```js
            `Review round ${round} of increment ${n}. ` +
            (priorFindings.length ? correctionScope : incrementRange) +
            scope(task, increments, n) +
            checkList(lastChecks) +
            `Read nothing out of ${dir}/backlog.json — not with the helper, not by hand.\n` +
            recordStep(task.id, reviewLabel, VERDICT_PAYLOAD),
```

`scope`, `checkList`, the "read nothing" line and `recordStep` stay for every round: the
correction round still runs the closed list of commands, still needs the criteria to name a
violation against, and still reads nothing.

The correction prompt names the fix diff and no other range — naming the increment range beside
it would re-open the ground the round before ruled on, which is the convergence this issue is
about.

Two guards, both deliberate:
- `priorFindings.length` is what switches the form, not `round > 0`. A resumed run replays a
  recorded review from the index's steering projection, which drops the findings (see the
  rejected option above), so after a restart a correction round is dispatched in the first
  round's form — the review it would have had before this change, not a prompt that names
  nothing. Say that in the comment.
- An empty `head` falls back to the increment's range, so the prompt never renders
  `git diff ..HEAD` or the string `undefined`. The findings are still named.

Capture `previousVerdict` into a `const` rather than reading `verdict` inside the dispatch
closure: `verdict` is reassigned by the very statement that awaits the dispatch, and a `const`
makes it impossible for a later edit to reorder that into a self-reference.

## 3. `agents/reviewer.md` — what a correction round asks of the reviewer

Frontmatter `description`: after the clause about the diff range its prompt names, add that in a
correction round the prompt names instead the findings the round before filed and the diff of the
fix, and that it verdicts each of those findings. One clause; the description is read far more
often than the body.

Body, the paragraph at lines 19-23 ("The diff your prompt names is your whole context…"): keep it
and add that in a correction round the range the prompt names is the fix's.

Body, lines 25-29: keep "Read the issue file whole before you read the diff: you review what was
asked for, not what was built." Delete the rest of that paragraph — "Every round starts fresh,
this one included… A round that re-checks only its own list inherits its own blind spots." — and
put in its place: the prompt names the round; the first round of an increment is the whole
increment and reviews the intent whole; a later round is a correction round, and the section
below is what it asks. That deleted sentence is the direct contradiction of this change, and a
page that adds the new section while leaving it standing forbids in one breath what it just
asked for.

Add a section `## A correction round`, after `## What you check` and before `## The reproduction
rule`. One rule per paragraph — the suite pins each rule to the paragraph that carries it:

- What it is: a correction round exists to answer the findings the round before filed. The prompt
  names those findings and the diff of the fix, and those two are the whole of what you judge:
  the increment as a whole was ruled on in the round that filed them.
- Addressed: verdict every named finding as addressed or not addressed. Addressed means the
  defect no longer exists — you ran its reproduction again and it is gone. A fix that was
  attempted, a comment that says it was handled, a test that now names it: none of those is
  addressed while the defect stands. A finding you verdict not addressed you file again, with
  what you found this time as its reproduction, classified like any other.
- New breakage: what the fix itself broke, inside the fix diff, is a finding. Judge that diff by
  the four checks above, the listed commands included.
- Observations: a remark outside the named findings and outside the fix diff is an observation,
  however true it is — it goes in `summary`, it does not block the increment and it does not
  start another round. The round before ruled on that ground, and re-opening it is what keeps a
  loop from converging.
- The count: `findingCount` counts the findings you verdicted not addressed and the new ones
  inside the fix diff, and nothing else.
- The summary: say, per named finding, addressed or not.

`## What you record`: amend two bullets and add one.
- The `findings` bullet: a re-filed finding carries what you found this round as its
  reproduction.
- The `findingCount` / `allDirect` bullet: the sentence "the findings themselves it never sees,
  because whoever corrects them reads them out of the state" is no longer true. Your caller
  carries your findings into the next round's review prompt, because that round's reviewer reads
  nothing either, and it does nothing else with them.
- A `head` bullet: the commit your checkout was on while you reviewed, from
  `git rev-parse HEAD`. The round after is dispatched against `<head>..HEAD`, so the fix's diff
  is exactly what landed after you looked.

## What is deliberately left alone

- `README.md`: "review findings open a correction round; after two the loop stops" is still true,
  and the agent table's "handed nothing any other agent produced" still holds — what a correction
  round's reviewer is handed is what the reviewer role itself filed, not another agent's work.
- `INDEX_STEP` and the `STATE` schema in the workflow: adding `head` there would let a resumed
  correction round name the fix range, but without the findings it would still be dispatched in
  the first round's form, so the field would buy nothing.
- `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs` and `hooks/read-barrier.mjs`: unchanged. The reviewer
  still reads nothing, so the barrier still fits, and the recorder needs no new field — `head` is
  a short string and its steering projection already accepts one.
- `MAX_CORRECTIONS`, the direct-fix fast path, and every other round's dispatch.

Tests are needed. Everything this increment changes is either behaviour of the dispatch the

## The suite doc

No `CLAUDE.md` governs `test-repo.sh` — the suite-doc check in that same file only requires one
for a directory holding a `*.test.mjs`, and shell suites have never had one. Its conventions are
in the file itself: a section opened with `echo "=== …"`, a comment above each case saying what it
pins and why, `ok "<sentence>"` / `no "<sentence>"` per case, and, inside the driver heredoc,
`assertTrue(<condition>, '<what is wrong when it fails>')` with the message written as the defect,
not as the expectation. Follow those.

Do not write a suite doc for it. A `CLAUDE.md` at the repository root would load as project memory
and be inherited by every subagent this session dispatches, which `.claude/rules/agents.md`
forbids in as many words; record the absence in your return instead.

## Fixtures to extend first

In the driver heredoc, `verdictReturnWithFinding` (line 627) is the verdict every correction-round
case runs on. Give it the two new fields, with markers in the file's style:

```js
const verdictReturnWithFinding = {
  findingCount: 1,
  allDirect: false,
  reason: 'MARKER-VERDICT-REASON',
  findings: [
    { claim: 'MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM', reproduction: 'MARKER-FINDING-REPRO', criterion: 'does i1' },
  ],
  head: 'MARKER-REVIEW-HEAD',
  questions: [],
  summary: 'verdict summary',
};
```

Add `MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM`, `MARKER-FINDING-REPRO` and `MARKER-REVIEW-HEAD` to
`DISJOINT_MARKERS` (line ~580), which is the list the harness proves pairwise substring-disjoint
before it runs anything. `verdictReturnWithDirectFinding` derives from this fixture and inherits
both fields, so w16 and w24 keep working unchanged.

Leave `idxStep` (line 656) alone. It projects only the steering values the real index carries, so
a fixture verdict replayed from the state naturally arrives without `findings` and without
`head` — which is exactly the resumed case w27 below exists for.

## Case A — mode `w26`: a correction round is dispatched against the findings and the fix diff

Level: integration, through the workflow driver. Context: the same as `w10` —
`{ stateReturn: noState, decomposeReturn: decomposeReturnOne, researchReturn: planReturn,
verdictFor: (label) => (label === 'review:i1.0' ? verdictReturnWithFinding : verdictReturnClean) }`.
Register it in the `for wf` loop beside the others:
`run_driver "$wf" w26 "$wf_name: a correction round's review is dispatched against the findings and the fix's diff"`.

Assert the label sequence is the one-correction-round sequence `w10` already expects, then, on
`review:i1.1`:

1. The prompt contains `MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM` and `MARKER-FINDING-REPRO`. Criterion 1. Break:
   drop `findingList(priorFindings)` from the correction block, and the reviewer is told a
   correction round happened without being told what it corrects.
2. The prompt contains `git diff MARKER-REVIEW-HEAD..HEAD`. Criterion 1. Break: leave the review
   dispatch naming the increment range for every round.
3. The prompt does not contain `git diff issue-branch...HEAD`. Criteria 1 and 4 — the round judges
   the fix, not the increment again. Break: name both ranges in the correction prompt.
4. The prompt matches `/correction round/i`. Criteria 2-5: every rule the page carries is keyed on
   the round being a correction round, so a prompt that hands over findings without saying what
   kind of round it is leaves the page unreachable. Break: paste the findings under the ordinary
   round heading.
5. The prompt contains no `steps docs/issues/x/backlog.json` and still matches
   `/read nothing out of/i`. Criterion 6. Break: replace the pasted findings with a `steps … i1
   review:i1.0 --fields findings` read.
6. The prompt contains `CHECK-MARKER`. Blast radius: the closed list of commands has to survive
   into the correction round, or the reviewer runs nothing. Break: build the correction prompt
   without `checkList(lastChecks)`.

And on `review:i1.0`, in the same mode:

7. The prompt contains `git diff issue-branch...HEAD`, does not contain `MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM`,
   and does not match `/correction round/i`. Criterion 7. Break: switch the form on `round > 0`
   alone in a way that also fires at round 0, or make `incrementRange` render differently.
8. The prompt contains the recorded-field lines `` - `findings` `` and `` - `head` ``.
   Criteria 1 and 5: the state has to keep the findings and the commit reviewed, which is what
   `VERDICT_PAYLOAD` names. Break: add `head` to the schema and forget it in `VERDICT_PAYLOAD`.

9. In the same branch, assert on the workflow source the driver already holds in `src`: the
   `const VERDICT = { … }` block names `findings` and `head`, and its `required:` line lists both.
   The driver stubs every agent return, so a schema that never asks the reviewer for these two
   would leave every assertion above green while the real run got neither. Criterion 1. Break:
   build the prompt from `verdict.findings` and `verdict.head` without adding them to `VERDICT`.

## Case B — mode `w27`: a correction round resumed from the state falls back to the first round's form

Level: integration, through the workflow driver. Context: a state fixture in the style of
`resumeState()`, holding increment `i1` on branch `issue-branch--i1` with round 0 complete —
`idxStep('research:i1.0', planReturn)`, `idxStep('tests:i1.0', testsReturn)`,
`idxStep('implement:i1.0', buildReturn)`, `idxStep('review:i1.0', verdictReturnWithFinding)` — and
`[idxStep('decompose', decomposeReturnOne)]` as the run steps. `idxStep` drops `findings` and
`head`, which is the point: this is what a restart really leaves behind. Register it as
`run_driver "$wf" w27 "$wf_name: a correction round resumed from the state is dispatched as a first round, not as a broken one"`.

Assert the labels are
`['load-state', 'research:i1.1', 'tests:i1.1', 'implement:i1.1', 'review:i1.1', 'replan:i1', 'publish']`,
then on `review:i1.1`:

1. The prompt contains `git diff issue-branch...HEAD`. The empty edge: with no findings in hand
   the round is dispatched exactly as a first round. Break: switch the form on `round > 0` instead
   of on the findings actually being there.
2. The prompt contains neither `undefined` nor `git diff ..HEAD`. The other empty edge — a
   correction form built from values a restart dropped renders a git command nobody can run.
   Break: build the fix range from `previousVerdict.head` without the fallback.
3. The prompt does not match `/correction round/i`. Same decision, from the other side: a prompt
   that announces a correction round and then names no finding asks the reviewer for a verdict on
   a list it does not have. Break: emit `correctionScope` whenever `round > 0`.

## Case C — the rules on `agents/reviewer.md`

A new section in `test-repo.sh`, `echo "=== a correction round judges the fix"`, placed after the
`=== the reviewer proves a doubt with a probe in the sandbox` section and built the same way: a
`declare -a` table of `heading-pattern:label:term:term:…` rules, each resolved with the same `awk`
paragraph extraction (`-v RS=''`, entering on `^## ` matching the heading pattern) and successive
`grep -iE` filters, collecting the labels that match no paragraph. That style is deliberate and
the comment above the existing table says why: a flat page-wide grep passes on words the
frontmatter already carries, so each rule is pinned to one paragraph of the section that owns it.

One rule per criterion, each with terms chosen so only the paragraph carrying that rule satisfies
all of them:

1. Criterion 2 — the paragraph under the correction-round heading that carries `addressed`,
   `no longer exists` and `attempt`. Break: delete that paragraph, or soften it to "a fix was
   made", and the reviewer may verdict an attempt as addressed.
2. Criterion 3 — the paragraph carrying `fix`, `diff` and `finding` together with
   `broke|breakage|introduc`. Break: delete it, and new breakage inside the fix reads as an
   observation.
3. Criterion 4 — the paragraph carrying `observation`, `summary`, `outside` and `round`. Break:
   delete it, and any true remark re-opens the increment and extends the loop.
4. Criterion 5 — the paragraph carrying `findingcount` and `not addressed|not-addressed`. Break:
   delete it, and the count sweeps in observations, so an accepted fix still opens a round.
5. Criterion 1, the page's side — the paragraph carrying `prompt`, `finding` and `diff`, which is
   what tells the reviewer where the two things the workflow now sends it are. Break: delete it,
   and the pasted findings arrive with nothing saying they are the scope.

Two negative cases in the same section, each in the shape of the existing
"old blanket prohibition" case (`grep -inE … || true`, empty output is the pass):

6. `grep -inE 'every round starts fresh|knows nothing of the earlier ones' agents/reviewer.md`
   finds nothing. Criteria 2-5: a page that adds the correction-round section while keeping the
   sentence that every round re-reviews the whole intent afresh contradicts itself, and the
   reader follows whichever it saw last. Break: add the section and leave the old paragraph
   standing.
7. `grep -inE 'the findings themselves it never sees' agents/reviewer.md` finds nothing.
   Criterion 1: the caller now carries the findings into the next review prompt, so a page still
   promising it never sees them is a false statement about the channel this change builds. Break:
   extend `VERDICT` and leave the `findingCount`/`allDirect` bullet as it was.

## What is left untested, and why

- The reviewer's own behaviour once dispatched — that it really re-runs a reproduction before
  verdicting a finding addressed — is a model behaviour no tool in this repository can assert.
  Criteria 2-5 are tested as the rules the page carries, which is how every other rule of an
  agent page is pinned here.
- `git rev-parse HEAD` actually returning the reviewed commit is the agent's action at run time;
  the suite pins that the schema asks for it, that the state records it, and that the next round's
  prompt is built from it.
- The whole-suite regression of the other 24 driver modes is not a case of its own: they run in
  the same command, and `w16`/`w24` cover the fixture the two new fields are added to.

## What is already red

Nothing was run for this plan, and no baseline was taken: a run buys no fact the reading did not
already give. Expect `bash test-repo.sh` to be green on the tree as it stands, and expect the new
cases to be red until the two production files change — the driver executes
`workflows/agile-loop.js` as written, so cases A and B fail on the prompt as it is today, and
case C fails on the page as it is today. The first run of the list belongs to whoever runs it
downstream.
return.summary: A correction round’s reviewer is dispatched against the previous round’s findings and the fix’s diff range, which travel in its prompt because it reads nothing: the verdict schema gains the findings and the commit reviewed, and agents/reviewer.md gains the rules for verdicting each finding addressed or not, counting only those and new fix-diff breakage, and parking everything else as an observation.
